findings.quote: a sustained break would open 6150-6315, about a 20% correction from the peak
findings.why: The JPMorgan technical outlook in the context gives only the 6800-7000 support and says a sustained break would signal a cyclical bear market; 6150-6315 and a 20% correction appear nowhere.
findings.fix: Drop the 6150-6315 and 20% figures and say a sustained break below 6800-7000 would signal a cyclical bear market.

findings.quote: three-month copper on the London exchange broke trend support at 13800-14050
findings.why: The context says only that copper broke pattern support (JPMorgan) and plunged on the LME (Natixis); no 13800-14050 level appears.
findings.fix: Remove the 13800-14050 level and say copper broke pattern support.

findings.quote: with gold well below critical support at 3800-4000 and a sustained break there implying a measured move to the mid-$2,000s
findings.why: No JPMorgan entry carries a 3800-4000 gold support zone or a mid-$2,000s measured move; the only JPMorgan gold level in the context is support at $3605.
findings.fix: Delete the 3800-4000 and mid-$2,000s figures or replace the sentence with a claim the context carries.

findings.quote: In past shocks volatility took 6 to 8 weeks to subside, and outside recessions the S&P 500 fell a further 14% to 16%.
findings.why: The Deutsche Bank positioning note in the context describes the vol shock and a median -24% recession selloff but has no 6-to-8-week or 14%-16% figure.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence or replace it with Deutsche Bank's stated point that the market is halfway to a typical recession selloff (median -24%).

findings.quote: a jump of more than 1.5 standard deviations
findings.why: The Deutsche Bank entry names a vol shock with measures in the top decile but gives no 1.5 standard deviation definition.

findings.quote: with systematic strategies at their biggest underweight in 18 months
findings.why: Deutsche Bank's entry says CTA equity allocation is at a seven-month low (36th percentile) and vol-control funds at the 21st percentile; no 18-month figure appears.
findings.fix: Say CTA equity allocation is at a seven-month low and vol-control funds are at the 21st percentile.

findings.why: Natixis says it favors buying dips in the long end and that entry level is critical, with a 4.90%-5.25% range; no 5.20%-5.25% entry level is stated.
findings.fix: Say Natixis favors buying dips in long-dated bonds but treats the entry level as critical, without the 5.20%-5.25% figure.

findings.quote: while Natixis does not expect 50bp but does expect a hawkish meeting that keeps January well priced
findings.why: The Natixis entries say only that Fed speakers are hawkish with focus on the size of the December hike; no Natixis view on 50bp or January pricing appears (JPMorgan's briefing is the one calling 50bp unlikely).
findings.fix: Drop the Natixis clause or attribute the 50bp-unlikely view to JPMorgan.

findings.quote: wants last year's three insurance cuts reversed
findings.why: Every Waller reference in the context covers his call for a 50bp December hike or a faster pace; none says he wants the 2025 cuts reversed.
findings.fix: Cut the clause and keep only that Waller is advocating 50bp in December.

findings.quote: expects the market to rebound as catalysts clear
findings.why: JPMorgan's View note stays constructive into 2027 and its briefings are tactically bullish on cleaner positioning, but no entry says it expects a rebound as catalysts clear, and the View says it would fade the cyclicals bounce.
findings.fix: Say JPMorgan remains tactically bullish on cleaner positioning instead of forecasting a rebound as catalysts clear.
